newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, Suriname VPs hold meeting in Nicaragua.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, Suriname VPs hold meeting in Nicaragua.

text.p: The vice-presidents of Taiwan and Suriname, which do not have diplomatic ties, have met secretly in Nicaragua, Taipei media reported on Sunday.

"Vice-president Lien Chan had held a secret meeting with Suriname vice-president," the Central Daily News, owned by the ruling Nationalist Party, reported from Nicaragua where Lien is conducting an official visit.
Suriname recognises Beijing's communist government, Taiwan's political rival after a civil war separated them in 1949.
"The two sides stress that they will strengthen cooperation," the newspaper said. "International friendship is waiting for the Republic of China."
Lien is in Nicaragua, one of only 30 countries that recognise Taipei's Republic of China government, for the inauguration of Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman.

Suriname was interested in establishing ties with Taiwan more than 10 years ago, eyeing the cash-flush island's financial aid, but pressure from China made such a move impossible, reported the United Daily News, one of Taiwan's two biggest newspapers.
"The meeting between the two vice-presidents this time should help relations between the two countries," it said.
Beijing has tightened a diplomatic squeeze on Taipei since 1949 in its quest to bring Taiwan under mainland rule.
Taiwan says it does not want independence, but insists that the island has the right to develop its own foreign relations before reunification can be realised.

Lien, who also doubles as Taiwan premier, is scheduled to visit the Vatican, which also recognises Taiwan. He will meet with Pope John Paul before returning to Taipei from Nicaragua, Taiwan Foreign Minister John Chang has said.
Lien would invite the Pope to visit Taiwan during their meeting, the Liberty Times newspaper reported.
Beijing has expressed a desire to improve ties with the Vatican, but said the Holy See first would have to sever links with Taiwan.
